sentences.text:
The petitioner is the accused in S.C.No.435/2025 on the files of the Fast Track Special Court (POCSO), Kunnamkulam, which arose out of Crime No.338/2024 of Peramangalam Police Station,
Thrissur.

The offences alleged against him are under Sections 341, 323, 376, 376(2)(n) & 506(i) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.
The prosecution case is that the petitioner/accused indulged in sexual relationship with the de facto complainant from 01.11.2022 to 10.05.2024, giving the false promise of marriage to her.
It is also alleged that on one occasion, the petitioner had inflicted voluntary hurt upon the de facto complainant and criminally intimidated her.
3. In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that he is totally innocent, and that he has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further stated that his relationship with the de facto complainant was purely consensual, and hence the offence of rape is not attracted.

According to the petitioner, the de facto complainant/second respondent had sworn an affidavit stating that the matter has been amicably settled, and that she has no objection in quashing the proceedings against him.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned counsel for the second respondent/de facto complainant and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

5. It is apparent from the facts of the case that at the time when the petitioner and the second respondent indulged in sexual relationship, both of them were married to other persons, and they were having children also.
Therefore, the contention of the de facto complainant that she had extended consent for sexual relationship believing the offer of marriage given by the petitioner, is prima facie unacceptable.
That apart, it is seen from the affidavit filed by the de facto complainant that she had acknowledged the fact that her relationship with the petitioner was purely consensual.

6. The learned public prosecutor, upon instructions, submitted that the de facto complainant had given a statement to the Investigating Officer also to the effect that the issue has been amicably settled with the petitioner, and that she is not at all interested in continuing the prosecution against the petitioner.

7. The learned counsel for the de facto complainant submitted that the complaint happened to be preferred due to a misunderstanding 2025:KER:59544 and mistake, and that there was consensual relationship between the petitioner and the de facto complainant as part of their friendship.

sentences.text: Having regard to the above facts and circumstances of this case, it is not possible to say that the petitioner has committed the offence of rape against the de facto complainant/second respondent.
So also, the prosecution records do not disclose the other offences of criminal intimidation and inflicting voluntary hurt alleged to have been committed by the petitioner.
In that view of the matter, the prayer of the petitioner to quash the proceedings against him, has to be allowed.
In the result, the petition stands allowed.

The proceedings against the petitioner (accused) in S.C.No.435/2025 on the files of the Fast Track Special Court (POCSO), Kunnamkulam, which arose out of Crime No.338/2024 of Peramangalam Police Station, Thrissur, are hereby quashed.

(Sd/-)
